title: An hour of prayer (II.1)
hookLine: he recommends a daily hour of mental prayer, early if possible
tomorrow: how do you take a prayer with you when you leave?

lines: ROOM FOR THE LIFE YOU HAVE.
cards: The weekly screen-time report lands like a verdict: hours, every day, on one small glass rectangle. So when Francis de Sales asks for one hour a day of prayer, the honest reaction is: who has that?
Part two of his book turns to prayer, and it opens on exactly that number. Then, in the same breath, he makes room for the life you actually have.

teach.b: The question is simple: when should a person pray? De Sales recommends mental prayer, the prayer of the heart, above all on the life and passion of Jesus.
Children learn to speak by listening to their mothers, he says; we learn Christ's ways by keeping company with him.

teach.h: AN HOUR, EARLY IF YOU CAN.
teach.b: An hour a day, and no more without your guide's advice. Early in the morning if you can, when the mind is fresh after the night.

teach.h: IF THE MORNING'S LOST, MAKE IT UP.
teach.b: If the morning gets swallowed, make it up later, though not right after a meal, when you'd only be drowsy. And if the whole day slips, repair it with short prayers and begin again. Now a neighbor who also prizes the dawn.

teach.h: THE QUR'AN: THE DAWN IS WITNESSED.
teach.b: In the Qur'an, God tells the Prophet to keep up the prayer from the sun's decline into the dark of night, and the recitation at dawn, which the verse says is witnessed.
Here's the shared thing to tell a friend: two traditions, two languages, both pointing at first light.
And one honest difference: salah, the Muslim ritual prayer, has set words and movements at set times; de Sales's hour is mostly silent prayer of the heart, and its time can move.

how: Some Catholics keep a daily time of mental prayer, often in the morning, and the Church's Liturgy of the Hours sets morning and evening prayer at the hinges of the day.

s: de Sales says an hour or nothing; less doesn't count
if the morning's lost, make it up later; if the day slips, short prayers and begin again.
de Sales and the Qur'an both point to the dawn
early if you can, de Sales says; the Qur'an speaks of the recitation at dawn as witnessed.
Muslim salah and de Sales's mental prayer are the same practice
salah has set words and movements at set times; de Sales's hour is mostly silent and can move.

games.q: you planned to pray at 6am, slept through the alarm, and now it's noon and you just ate lunch. what would de Sales suggest?
o: make it up later in the day, once you're not drowsy from the meal.
skip today; the morning was the whole point.
pray right now, while you're full and relaxed.
games.why: early if you can, he says; if the morning is lost, make it up later, but not right after a meal.

practice: Let these two minutes be the first small slice of that hour. Say the Our Father out loud, slowly, one phrase per breath, and when a phrase holds you, stop there and stay.
If you don't pray, say one line you love, aloud, the same way.

wordCard.voice: An hour of prayer. Francis de Sales's counsel: a daily hour of mental prayer, early if possible, made up later if the morning is lost.

carryVoice: Pocket this one: an hour, if you can, and the if is part of the counsel. That's day 1497.
